verses.28: The word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:
verses.29: "Set out for the great city of Nineveh, and announce to it the message that I will tell you."
verses.30: So Jonah made ready and went to Nineveh, according to the LORD'S bidding. Now Nineveh was an enormously large city; it took three days to go through it.
verses.31: Jonah began his journey through the city, and had gone but a single day's walk announcing, "Forty days more and Nineveh shall be destroyed,"
verses.32: when the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast and all of them, great and small, put on sackcloth.
verses.33: When the news reached the king of Nineveh, he rose from his throne, laid aside his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in the ashes.
verses.34: Then he had this proclaimed throughout Nineveh, by decree of the king and his nobles: "Neither man nor beast, neither cattle nor sheep, shall taste anything; they shall not eat, nor shall they drink water.
verses.35: Man and beast shall be covered with sackcloth and call loudly to God; every man shall turn from his evil way and from the violence he has in hand.
verses.36: Who knows, God may relent and forgive, and withhold his blazing wrath, so that we shall not perish."
verses.37: When God saw by their actions how they turned from their evil way, he repented of the evil that he had threatened to do to them; he did not carry it out.
verses.38: But this was greatly displeasing to Jonah, and he became angry.
verses.39: "I beseech you, LORD," he prayed, "is not this what I said while I was still in my own country? This is why I fled at first to Tarshish. I knew that you are a gracious and merciful God, slow to anger, rich in clemency, loathe to punish.
verses.40: And now, LORD, please take my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live."
verses.41: But the LORD asked, "Have you reason to be angry?"
verses.42: Jonah then left the city for a place to the east of it, where he built himself a hut and waited under it in the shade, to see what would happen to the city.
verses.43: And when the LORD God provided a gourd plant, that grew up over Jonah's head, giving shade that relieved him of any discomfort, Jonah was very happy over the plant.
verses.44: But the next morning at dawn God sent a worm which attacked the plant, so that it withered.
verses.45: And when the sun arose, God sent a burning east wind; and the sun beat upon Jonah's head till he became faint. Then he asked for death, saying, "I would be better off dead than alive."
verses.46: But God said to Jonah, "Have you reason to be angry over the plant?" "I have reason to be angry," Jonah answered, "angry enough to die."
verses.47: Then the LORD said, "You are concerned over the plant which cost you no labor and which you did not raise; it came up in one night and in one night it perished.
verses.48: And should I not be concerned over Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons who cannot distinguish their right hand from their left, not to mention the many cattle?"
